title: Trajectory Econ Watershed Benchmark (draft)
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a working draft of a compact benchmark report that compares end-to-end latency and per-token unit cost across a set of operational "watershed" scenarios we think are representative of production workloads. The goal is to create a single-page explainer (with lightweight charts in text form) that product, SRE, and sales can iterate on for tradeoff discussions. Not a final slide — intentionally conversational with open questions.

Key ideas / hypothesis:
- There are ~3 dominant operational regimes that drive different cost/latency tradeoffs: interactive short-turn dialogs (low token counts but tight p99), sessionized long conversations (high cumulative tokens where caching helps), and bursty background generation (high throughput, can tolerate higher p95).
- Quantization + prefix KV caching yields most of the cost savings on sessionized workloads but has diminishing returns on ultra-short interactive workloads where p99 is dominated by tail scheduling and prewarm penalties.

Experiment configuration (canonical runs):
- Models: redwood-mini-7B (float32), redwood-mini-7B-quant8, redwood-13B-8bit, redwood-13B-quant4 (toy variants for parity with internal suite)
- Hardware: H100x1 (core region), A100-40GBx1 (edge sim), T4x1 (legacy target) — see notes below for exact instance types used in each run
- Client pattern: three synthetic workload profiles (see below). Each run = 30m steady-state after 10m warmup.
- Batching: continuous batching ON (default policy) unless noted. KV cache ON for sessionized tests, OFF for stateless tests.
- Metric definitions: p50/p90/p99 latency (in ms) measured from client-observed request start to first-token-emitted and to last-token-emitted for end-to-end; cost computed as $ per 1M generated tokens using internal cost model (incl. infra amortization).

Workload profiles:
1) Short-Interactive (SI): 300 req/min, avg prompt+response token = 60 tokens, real-time constraint. Characteristic: p99 target < 250 ms for first token.
2) Sessionized Conversation (SC): 60 sessions/min, avg session length 1,200 generated tokens spread across turns (cumulative caching effect). Mix of LRU-friendly prefixes.
3) Bursty Bulk (BB): 2 large jobs/min, each job = 8k tokens, client tolerates higher p95 but wants throughput. Emulates batchembedding-like generation.

Representative text charts (ASCII) — latency vs cost per scenario
Note: each scenario shows three model variants: 7B-fp32 (A), 7B-q8 (B), 13B-q4 (C). Cost units = $/1M tokens (right axis). Latency = p95 first-token in ms (left axis).

SI (Short-Interactive) snapshot:
  Model | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | cost($/1M)
  ------------------------------------------------
  A 7B-fp32  |   55   |   210   |   430   |  420
  B 7B-q8   |   60   |   230   |   480   |  320
  C 13B-q4  |   75   |   260   |   560   |  610

ASCII mini-chart (p95 vs cost):
   p95(ms) 
  600 |                    C
  500 |           C
  400 |    A  B
  300 |    A  B
  200 | A  B
      +--------------------------------
        200  300  400  500  600  cost($/1M)

Observation (SI): quant helps cost substantially but p99 tails are still dominated by scheduling/warmup behavior. 7B-q8 gives the best cost with acceptable interactive p95; 13B-q4 reduces model mismatch but at cost premium and worse p99.

SC (Sessionized Conversation) snapshot:
  Model | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | cost($/1M)
  ------------------------------------------------
  A 7B-fp32  |   70   |   300   |   540   |  380
  B 7B-q8   |   75   |   320   |   560   |  210
  C 13B-q4  |   95   |   360   |   640   |  360

ASCII trend (relative cost reduction from caching):
   scenario: SC
   Baseline cost (no cache) = 480 for 7B-fp32
   With KV cache hit 45%: cost -> 380 (20% savings)
   With quant + cache: 7B-q8 cost -> 210 (56% savings vs baseline)

Observation (SC): caching multiplies with quantization. Large wins in cumulative token unit economics. p95/p99 also improve because fewer tokens are generated per turn (prefix cached).

BB (Bursty Bulk) snapshot:
  Model | throughput(tk/s) | p50(ms per token) | cost($/1M)
  ----------------------------------------------------------
  A 7B-fp32  |  450  |   2.2  |  350
  B 7B-q8   |  510  |   1.9  |  260
  C 13B-q4  |  420  |   2.7  |  480

Observation (BB): throughput-oriented runs favor quantized medium models; 7B-q8 gives highest sustained tokens/sec. 13B variants show lower throughput per GPU and higher unit cost for pure bulk jobs.

Cross-scenario synthesis (high level):
- If customer SLAs prioritise p99-first-token < 300 ms, prefer dedicated prewarmed pools on H100 and conservative quant profiles; caching has limited impact for single-turn SI workloads so scheduling/warmup and regional routing are the main levers.
- If workload is sessionized with repeated prefixes, enable KV caching + quantization aggressively: this is where the largest % savings manifest (30–60% unit cost drop).
- For planned heavy batch jobs, prefer cheaper hardware options with larger batch windows and aggressive quantization; throughput dominates rather than p99.

Open questions / notes to investigate next iterations:
- Tail decomposition: in SI p99 we need a tracewalk to separate prewarm scheduling tails vs kernel-level slow-paths — add a p99 attribution run (JIRA-OBS-3439).
- Quant artifacts: observed occasional hallucination rate increase in 13B-q4 under long-scrolling sessions — add QA prompt-set checks and BLEU/ROUGE-style regression tests before recommending q4 for sessionized production.
- Edge vs core: run the same SI profile on A100-edge instances with 5% background network jitter to validate region routing behavior.

Replication notes and commands (internal):
- run id: obs-traj-20270303
- benchmark harness: internal/tooling/bench/runner_v2
- sample invocation: ./runner_v2 --workload SI --model redwood-mini-7B-quant8 --instances H100 --duration 2400 --warmup 600 --collect p50,p95,p99,cost
- raw logs and summarized CSVs: see linked_artifacts above + s3://redwood-bench/obs/trajectory/2027-03-03/

Recommend next steps for collateralization:
- Convert table snapshots into two simple slides: 1) three-scenario tradeoff, 2) recommended default profiles and guardrails (when to enable q8 vs q4 and when to require prewarm).
- Run a short controlled customer-facing vignette using a real prompt-set (one enterprise customer workload) to validate cost regressions before publishing.
- Move this doc to final once tail attribution run complete and we have edge vs core verification.

Notes (free-form):
- This doc intentionally mixes polished numbers with rough observations — please flag any suspicious cost numbers (I pulled infra amortization from back-of-envelope model B, not final billing).
- Quick ask: Liam — can you run the p99 attribution tracewalk for the SI profile and drop a short summary in comments? Jia — can you validate hallucination checks for 13B-q4 on the customer prompt set? Rafael — please sanity-check the cost-per-token model inputs (gpu-hour rates, pct-util assumptions).

End.
